name: SOUTH AFRICA

flag.title: South Africa
flag.note: Six colours, Y-shape, unique in the world

lead: South Africa sits at the tip of Africa, where the Atlantic and Indian oceans meet. It has snowy mountains, hot deserts, wild savannah and whale-filled seas. It has 12 official languages.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: roughly twice the size of France

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: South Africa wraps around Africa's southern tip. The flat Karoo desert spreads across the middle. The Drakensberg mountains form a giant wall in the east.
Two oceans touch its coast. The Atlantic is cold in the west. The Indian Ocean is warm in the east. They meet near Cape Agulhas, Africa's true southern tip.
animals: South Africa has the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo. You can spot them all in Kruger National Park, one of Africa's largest game reserves.
Southern right whales swim close to shore at Hermanus, the best place to watch them from land. Penguins waddle on Boulders Beach, 40 km from Cape Town.
culture: Greetings change every few kilometres. Zulu speakers say 'Sawubona'. Xhosa speakers say 'Molo'. Afrikaans speakers say 'Hallo'. Eleven languages share one country.
Families gather around charcoal fires for a braai (barbecue) every weekend. Rugby is almost a religion. The Springboks are World Cup champions.
history: San hunter-gatherers and Bantu-speaking farmers lived in southern Africa for thousands of years. Dutch settlers arrived in 1652. The British came next. Conflict reshaped the land.
Apartheid was a cruel system of racial separation. It lasted from 1948 until 1994. Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison, then became the first democratically elected president.
wows: Only South Africa has given up its own nuclear weapons by choice.
Johannesburg sits on the world's largest gold reef.
South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
Boulders Beach has over 3,000 wild African penguins.
South Africa produces around 80% of the world's platinum.
Limpopo's baobab trees live 2,000 years and store thousands of litres of water.
Table Mountain is about 600 million years old, older than the Himalayas.
